newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF says Greenspan welcomed Japan reform plan.
newsitem.headline: MOF says Greenspan welcomed Japan reform plan.

text.p: U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan on Monday welcomed Japan's plan to liberalise its financial markets within five years and urged its Finance Minister to accelerate the process, an official of Japan's Finance Ministry (MOF) told reporters.
Greenspan made the comments during a morning meeting with Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka.
Greenspan arrived in Japan on Sunday and was due to stay until Tuesday.

The official told reporters that Greenspan applauded Japan's initiative in drawing up financial market deregulation plans and explained that the U.S. financial industry went through the same process in 1975.

Although U.S. securities firms had been worried at the time that liberalisation of commission fees would affect their profits, they ended up with increased trading volume and the liberalisation proved a success, Greenspan was quoted as saying.
Greenspan and Mitsuzuka spent most of their time discussing financial market reforms and did not exchange views on macro-economic issues, the official said.
Asked whether the two talked about the foreign exchange market, the official said they had discussed the topic but he declined say what they discussed.
The official said Greenspan welcomed Japan's efforts to increase the independence of the Bank of Japan and to make its decision-making on monetary policy more transparent.
He also quoted Greenspan as saying that the European Union's move towards economic unity would create a larger economic power than Japan or the United States.
Greenspan said the age was approaching of three large currency regions and that integration to promote global financial expansion was necessary, the official said.
Mitsuzuka told Greenspan Japanese financial firms were steadily dealing with their bad-loan problem and that the financial system was capable of handling the situation, the official said.
Greenspan told Mitsuzuka Japan needed to tackle financial reform and the bad-loan issue simultaneously to improve its financial system effectively, the official said.
Greenspan is due to hold a news conference in Tokyo at 9.30 a.m. (0030 GMT) on Tuesday.
